# Dialogue features

_Last updated with AmiWind v0.0.60-dev3 (31 October 2026)._

<!-- Generated whole by tools/dialogue_features.py render from docs/dialogue-features.json; do not edit by hand. -->

What of the original's dialogue AmiWind does, row by row, against the original and OpenMW 0.51. v0.0.58 ships the dialogue feature-complete against the original and OpenMW 0.51 (decided for the project, 31 October 2026); a row that is not done blocks the release unless it carries the maintainer's written deferral.

**5 of 29 done**, 19 partial, 5 missing.

## Measured on the game data

tools/dialogue_lut.py on Morrowind.esm (the report's coverage block), 31 October 2026; the 114 RankRequirement conditions moved to live on 1 November 2026 (FACTION-RANK-58).

### Services

| Part | State | What | Proof | Missing | Register |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Services and Service Refusal | partial | Barter, Travel, Training, Spells, Spellmaking, Enchanting and Repair from the NPC's flags, with Service Refusal. | Travel: the window lists Travel for a travel provider (aw_scene.c AW_SceneTravelOffers, the travel table of TRAVEL-SERVICES-CHIM-51); choosing it first asks the speaker's Service Refusal under the conversation's conditions, says a refusal that holds, else closes the window and opens the travel menu. The use key on a provider opens the conversation, as in OpenMW (tests/test_dialogue_features.py). Training: the speaker's three best skills priced by iTrainingMod and the barter offer (aw_dial.c AW_DialTrainingPicks, AW_DialTrainingPrice, AW_DialBarterOffer, equal to the reference on a native sweep), unaffordable rows greyed, the NPC's skill and the governing attribute (SKIL records, in the table) checked, then the skill up by one, two hours passed and the conversation closed. | Training raises the skill but does not count toward level progress yet: it will once LEVEL-UP-58 lands (the hook is marked in aw_dialwin.c train()). The window's words are the game's own GMST texts copied into the table (fallback wording only when a master lacks one). Spells: OpenMW's list (the speaker's plain spells the player lacks, by name) priced max(1, cost x fSpellValueMult) through the offer, the cost by the game's rule (tools/mwscript/actors.py spell_cost, an ASPC section of the actor table); the player's spell changes are capped at 8 by the actor record, so a ninth bought spell is refused; NPCs with autocalculated spells do not get them yet (OpenMW autocalcspell). Barter: two plain pages, Buy (the merchant's stock, equipped things and gold aside) and Sell (the player's things, equipped ones aside), one thing a click at the game's offer, only the kinds the service flags trade (an enchanted thing with Magic Items); a merchant keeps 12 item changes (MERCHANT-ITEM-CAP-58) and a sold thing it does not stock is kept as sold to that merchant (in the saved game) and can be bought back (BARTER-SOLD-ITEM-LOST-58). Repair: the player's weapons and armour below full health (equipped ones too), by name, at the game's price for the missing points (aw_dial.c AW_DialRepairPrice, checked natively) through the offer; mending sets full condition. Spellmaking and Enchanting: their price and cost rules are in (aw_dial.c AW_DialSpellmakingCost/Price, AW_DialEnchantCosts, Points, CastCost, Price, Chance, Capacity; OpenMW's SpellCreationDialog and Enchanting, checked against the reference natively), not their windows yet. Spellmaking: the window is in: the player names the spell (typing), adds effects from the plain spells he knows and the spells he made, sets magnitude, duration, area and range (Left and Right, within what the magic effect allows), sees the point cost and price, and buys it into his made spells (64 at most, saved); the game's words throughout, every effect named by its game setting; the limits are the original editor's (magnitude 1 to 100, duration 1 to 1440, area 0 to 50: no game setting holds them, the source is the original's sliders as OpenMW keeps them). GetEffect (the scripts) resolves an effect by name through its own list, which spells three effects unlike the game's settings (Drain, Restore and Fortify Magicka against ...Spellpoints): harmless, since the game's scripts name only Blind, Chameleon, Fire Damage, Invisibility and Poison, all resolved to the right effect (checked on the three masters). Known gaps: the spell's success chance is not shown, add and remove effect are bare + and - (the game has no setting text for them), casting a made spell is not in yet. Enchanting: the window is in: the player names the item, picks one of his things that can take an enchantment (its enchantment points from the record, now in the item catalogue) and a filled soul gem, steps the cast style by OpenMW's rule (a constant effect needs iSoulAmountForConstantEffect), adds effects as in Spellmaking (a constant effect on the wearer), sees the points against the item's capacity, the cast cost, the enchanter's chance and the price, and buys: the item and the gem (Azura's Star stays) leave, the enchanted item (aw_made_N, 64 at most, saved) comes; at an enchanter it always succeeds, as in OpenMW. Not in yet: ranged and thrown weapons (the item catalogue carries melee weapons only). Casting a made spell and using a made item's enchantment wait on player casting, its own work item beside SPELL-EFFECTS-57 (the player cannot cast yet: no spell selection, magicka cost, success roll or targeting). When it comes, the effects the engine applies today are Fortify, Drain, Damage and Restore of an attribute, a skill, health, magicka or fatigue, Cure Common Disease and Cure Blight Disease, on Self; every other effect, Touch and Target delivery and Constant Effect items need their own work and must be refused with a message naming the effect, never silently. The window of Enchanting is then done; casting made spells and using made items is the next row's work. (the entries are listed from the NPC's service flags, now in the table: tools/dialogue_lut.py services_of, OpenMW getServices, read once per conversation; choosing one checks Service Refusal and then says it is not in this build yet); no in-game still (build hold). Waits on: LEVEL-UP-58, PLAYER-CASTING-59. | DIALOGUE-WINDOW-LAYOUT-57 |
